messages.subject: Stochastic volatility model parameter question
parts:
I have a question about stochastic volatility model. I'm looking at this file:

https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/misc/moving-avg/stochastic-volatility-optimized.stan

One of the parameters there is h_std, which is a vector of size T, the number of trading days. Thus, being in the parameters block it is included in the NUTS resampling procedure. This appears to slow the process down. Stan users guide in section 5.6 states:
"There is a substantial amount of computation involved for parameter variables in a Stan program at each leapfrog step within the HMC or NUTS samplers, and a bit more computation along with writes involved for saving the parameter values corresponding to a sample."

It makes sense. However in this case the most meaningful parameters are those three: mu, phi and sigma. I don't really care about the distribution of h_std every trading day. In addition to speed concerns, I'm also concerned that Stan would concentrate on getting all those h_std right and not on other important parameters.

Would it make sense to let only mu, phi and sigma to be the only model parameters and let h_std being regenerated every time a new sample is drawn? It doesn't seem to be possible though, since _rng functions are not allowed in either model or transformed parameters.

Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stochastic volatility model parameter question
parts:
Sorry for the long delay in answering. We've been busy with
grants and StanCon.

See below.

> On Jan 17, 2017, at 4:02 PM, Denis Perevalov <deni...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I have a question about stochastic volatility model. I'm looking at this file:
>
> https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/misc/moving-avg/stochastic-volatility-optimized.stan
>
> One of the parameters there is h_std, which is a vector of size T, the number of trading days. Thus, being in the parameters block it is included in the NUTS resampling procedure. This appears to slow the process down. Stan users guide in section 5.6 states:
> "There is a substantial amount of computation involved for parameter variables in a Stan program at each leapfrog step within the HMC or NUTS samplers, and a bit more computation along with writes involved for saving the parameter values corresponding to a sample."
>
> It makes sense. However in this case the most meaningful parameters are those three: mu, phi and sigma. I don't really care about the distribution of h_std every trading day. In addition to speed concerns, I'm also concerned that Stan would concentrate on getting all those h_std right and not on other important parameters.

If you can analytically marginalize out h_std then that should
be faster (it's a consequence of the Rao-Blackwell theorem).

But if you can't marginalize analytically, you'll have to leave
the parameters in and let MCMC do the marginalization for you
computationally. That is, you're stuck sampling h_std it if you want
the right posterior over the parameters you do care about, namely
draws for (mu, phi, sigma).

> Would it make sense to let only mu, phi and sigma to be the only model parameters and let h_std being regenerated every time a new sample is drawn? It doesn't seem to be possible though, since _rng functions are not allowed in either model or transformed parameters.

Doing things that way won't produce the right answer, which is
why we don't allow RNGs before the generated quantities block.
Bayesian inference relies on two-way information flow, whereas
the RNG approach only goes one way.

- Bob
